subject: Clarify CHF collection rail and intermediary fee responsibility
messages:
From: Heinrich Wolf <heinrich.wolf@acme-swiss.com>

Cc: payables@acme-swiss.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 08:12:00 +0200
Subject: CHF payment to Redwood — intermediary charges and invoice netting

Hi Ava / Marissa,

Quick one from our AP team — we're initiating payment for INV-2019 (CHF 24,000) today via our Swiss treasury. The sending bank has flagged that the outbound SWIFT may route through an intermediary and their system shows an expected intermediary charge of CHF 40 (will be deducted from the beneficiary).

Two asks:
1) Do you want us to instruct our bank to send with OUR vs SHA vs BEN? If we use OUR, we will absorb intermediary costs, but some corporate policy teams avoid OUR.
2) If the intermediary fee is debited by the correspondent (i.e., we send SHA and Redwood receives net), do you prefer to: a) receive net and we handle reconciliation on our side, or b) you gross-up/credit the invoice back to gross after you reconcile?

Please confirm preferred routing and any required account/reference fields we should include so the funds reach your ledger cleanly (nostro tag/reference fields). I've attached the bank trace excerpt and our payment instruction screen.

Thanks,
Heinrich
Heinrich Wolf
Head of Treasury, Acme Swiss GmbH
payables@acme-swiss.com

From: ava_chen@redwood.ai
To: Heinrich Wolf <heinrich.wolf@acme-swiss.com>, payables@acme-swiss.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 11:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: CHF payment to Redwood — intermediary charges and invoice netting

Hi Heinrich,

Thanks for the heads-up and for attaching the trace. Short answers below plus a couple of practical options so your AP can pick what fits internal controls.

Policy & recommendations (what we normally do):
- Preferred: Instruct sending bank to use OUR (sender pays). That ensures the full invoice amount posts to our account and avoids manual reconciliations. If that is not possible for compliance reasons on your side, SHA is acceptable but it may result in a small deduction by one or more intermediaries.
- If SHA/BEN is used and we receive net: we can post the net receipt to the invoice and then evaluate a one-time credit adjustment for bona fide intermediary fees, but we require: (a) the MT103/trace showing the deduction, and (b) matching invoice reference. We do not gross-up proactively without evidence.

Required remittance fields (please include exact reference text):
- Beneficiary: Redwood Inference Inc.
- Account (CHF nostro): [REDFR-CH-01] account 004-112233-9 (please use the exact account string in our remit template attached)
- SWIFT / Correspondent: UBSWCHZH80A (UBS Zurich) — include as preferred correspondent where possible
- Reference: Redwood INV-2019  (very important for auto-applied payments)

Attachments I am sending: remit_instructions_ubs_template.txt (simple copy-paste template for your bank) and sample_invoice_INV-2019.pdf. If you can send a screenshot or MT103 showing the deduction we’ll fast-track the credit review.

Options for you to choose:
A) Use OUR: we will consider payment final on receipt of full gross amount.
B) Use SHA/BEN and provide MT103: we will process net and, if deduction is confirmed and <= CHF 200, issue a one-time credit for the fee after validation. Anything above that will need finance sign-off.

Let us know which option the treasury team chooses and attach the payment confirmation when done.

Best,
Ava Chen
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ava_chen@redwood.ai

Attachments: remit_instructions_ubs_template.txt, sample_invoice_INV-2019.pdf

Hi Ava,

Thanks — our treasury prefers not to use OUR due to routing controls. We'll send SHA and expect a small intermediary deduction. I've attached the sending bank's preliminary payment confirmation (shows expected CHF 40 intermediary fee).

Two follow-ups:
- Please confirm whether the one-time credit will be applied automatically on submission of the MT103, or whether we need to open a ticket with your finance team.
- Also: our Tax/Compliance asked for a short note on VAT treatment for this transfer (invoice is outside Swiss VAT scope for your services). Can you confirm you will not be issuing a VAT gross-up or any VAT invoice change when you issue the credit? We need that for our tax file.

Heinrich

Ava / Connor — looping you in for finance/ops confirmation. Summary: Acme Swiss will send SHA and expect ~CHF 40 intermediary deduction. They asked whether we auto-credit on MT103 submission and whether any VAT/gross-up implications exist.

Proposed internal position:
- We will accept net receipts for under CHF 200 and issue a one-time operational credit equal to the intermediary deduction after receiving the MT103 (finance will book as "bank fees reimbursement"). No change to the original invoice value will be made; the credit is a separate line (no VAT implications on our side).
- Require process: customer uploads MT103 to HubSpot record HS-40291 or replies to finance@redwood.ai with attachment and our invoice reference; ops will validate and post credit within 5 business days.

Connor, can you confirm the account string we should be presenting as the preferred correspondent? I put UBSWCHZH80A in the draft but want to be sure this matches treasury. If we can recommend adding "please tag: Redwood INV-2019" that will help auto-match.

Marissa

Redwood Inference
